title: A Flood Cut Nepal's Power to Bangladesh. Now It's Back
description: On Friday, 23 October 2026, Nepal resumed exporting 40 MW of hydropower to Bangladesh through India's grid. The supply had stopped after the 26 August Bhotekoshi flood damaged the Trishuli and Chilime plants, so the Solu Khola and Kabeli B-1 plants now supply it instead, with approval from India's Central Electricity Authority. NEA also earned Rs 5.925 billion from 634 million units exported to India between mid-September and mid-October, up Rs 962 million on the same period last year.

beats.text: A flood cut this power line
beats.vo: In August, a flash flood cut Nepal's power exports to Bangladesh. On Friday, the electricity started flowing again.

beats.text: Nepal resumes 40 MW power exports to Bangladesh
beats.source: Source: Kathmandu Post, Ajker Patrika, Nepal News
beats.ticker: Supply routed through India's grid after the Bhotekoshi flood
beats.vo: Nepal is once again sending forty megawatts to Bangladesh, carried across India's transmission grid.

beats.text: Earned from power exports to India in one month
beats.vo: And India is buying too. From mid September to mid October, the N E A earned nearly six billion rupees from about six hundred thirty four million units. That's almost a billion more than a year ago.

beats.text: How Nepal rerouted around the damage
points: Solu Khola, Kabeli B-1 step in
beats.vo: The flood damaged Trishuli and Chilime, the two plants approved to supply Bangladesh. So Nepal named new ones, Solu Khola and Kabeli B one, and India's Central Electricity Authority signed off.

events.text: Five-year seasonal deal with Bangladesh signed

beats.vo: The five year deal, signed in twenty twenty four, sends power every year from mid June to mid November.

beats.text: A grid with backup plants turns surplus monsoon power into income
beats.vo: For engineers in Nepal, this is the takeaway. Monsoon surplus is only worth money if the grid can reroute it. Having backup plants kept the deal alive.

caption: Nepal's power is flowing to Bangladesh again — 40 MW, after an August flood cut the line. How it was rerouted 👇
